notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Rasmus Ristolainen is out and has missed the last 5 games. Jamie Drysdale has taken his spot beside Travis Sanheim. That pair has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 72:29 together, up from 23% with Ristolainen.
Nikita Grebenkin is out at least four months (back surgery) and has not played this season. Sean Couturier has taken his spot beside Owen Tippett and Trevor Zegras.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 43% of the team’s power-play time in 9 games, up from 2% last season.

Samuel Honzek is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Matt Coronato has taken his spot beside Mikael Backlund and Joel Farabee. That line has had 41% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 93:29 together.
Maxim Tsyplakov has been a scratch for the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. William Strömgren has taken his spot beside Adam Klapka and Jonathan Castagna.
Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 14 games.
Jonathan Huberdeau is out long term (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
William Strömgren was added to the roster on Oct 31 and has played beside Adam Klapka and Jonathan Castagna.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 17 games, up from 2% last season.

story.head: The Flames are going to test Dan Vladař early and often
paras: The Flyers (4-10-4) lost 3-2 to the Rangers on Thursday, and the Flames (7-9-1) lost 5-3 to Anaheim on Friday. Going in, the Flyers are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 29th in the NHL) and the Flames fifth in the Pacific (tied for 24th).

The Flyers haven’t played well, but their record (.333) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .387, and their finishing has held them back. The Flames’ record (.441) is about what their chances are worth.

The Flyers play slow, tight games (2nd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (30th). The Flames, by contrast, play fast, open games (2nd). The Flyers also block more shots than almost anyone (3rd), so the Flyers are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Flames’ shots. Philadelphia has scored 2.17 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. On the other side, the Flames take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and take more penalties than they draw (30th). Calgary has scored 2.47 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flyers.

Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 18 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Matvei Michkov (10 G / 3 A / 13 P in 18 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (6 G / 10 A / 16 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Matt Coronato (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 17 GP) is next in line.
Dan Vladař (3-4-2 / .883 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to go for Philadelphia. Devin Cooley (4-3-0 / .912 SV% in 7 GS) has been terrific for Calgary and is expected to start.
At home, Ryan Huska likes to send Strömgren, Castagna and Klapka out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Barkey, Couturier and Acciari.
